[[File:2D Wavefunction (2,1) Surface Plot.png|thumb|A second eigenfunction in a rectangular domain; the nodal line is visible at the bottom.]]

In [[mathematics]], the '''nodal line conjecture''' is a statement posed in 1967 by [[Lawrence E. Payne]] about the [[Laplacian]] [[partial differential equation]]. The original conjecture predicts that for the [[Dirichlet boundary condition|Dirichlet]] problem on a bounded two-dimensional domain, the second eigenfunction has a nodal line that meets the boundary of the domain. The general conjecture was proved false in 1997 by carving a large number of microscopic holes out of a disk,<ref>M. Hoffmann-Ostenhof, T. Hoffmann-Ostenhof, N. Nadirashvili (December 15, 1997) "The nodal line of the second eigenfunction of the Laplacian in R^2 can be closed" Duke Math. J. 90(3): 631-640. DOI: 10.1215/S0012-7094-97-09017-7</ref> a technique that simulates a [[Schrödinger equation|Schrödinger]] potential.<ref>D. Cioranescu and F. Murat. "Un terme étrange venu d'ailleurs", I and II. In Nonlinear Differential Equations and Their Applications, Collège de France Seminar, Vol. 60 and 70, Research Notes in Mathematics, pages 98–138, 154–178. Pitman, London, 1982–1983.</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BYF5TpeMqyo |title=Jaume de Dios Pont — Some Extreme Regimes of the Laplace Operator |date=2026-03-13 |last=Simons Foundation |access-date=2026-03-20 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

Other positive and negative results are known for various special cases of domains; in general, it remains an open problem to describe how simple the domain must be for the conjecture to hold.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dahne |first=Joel |last2=Gómez-Serrano |first2=Javier |last3=Hou |first3=Kimberly |date=2021-12-01 |title=A counterexample to Payne's nodal line conjecture with few holes |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1007570421002690 |journal=Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation |volume=103 |article-number=105957 |doi=10.1016/j.cnsns.2021.105957 |issn=1007-5704|arxiv=2103.02276 }}</ref>
